company_snapshot.so_what: SQM is a large, profitable buyer again, so a multi-site autonomy programme is affordable at its scale.

company_snapshot.claim: Since 27 December 2025, SQM's Salar de Atacama lithium business (formerly SQM Salar SpA / Litio Chile) has operated as Nova Andino Litio SpA (Novandino), a joint venture with Codelco that runs lithium activities in the Salar de Atacama until 2060.
company_snapshot.so_what: The Atacama lithium sites in the email now sit inside Novandino, so the deal is likely contracted and approved by Novandino rather than SQM corporate.
company_snapshot.verification_note: S18: '27 diciembre 2025 ... SQM Salar SpA también denominada Litio Chile pasó a denominarse Nova Andino Litio SpA'; S8: joint venture with Codelco 'in the Salar de Atacama until 2060'

company_snapshot.claim: In the first half of 2026 SQM reported revenues of US$4,228.5 million (up 103.4% year on year) and net income of US$1,024.7 million, with record quarterly lithium sales of over 84 thousand tonnes LCE in Q2 2026.
company_snapshot.so_what: A strong 2026 price recovery gives room for operating improvements going into the Q3 budget conversation.
company_snapshot.verification_note: S10: revenues 'US$4,228.5 million ... increase of 103.4%'; net income 'US$1,024.7 million'; 'record quarterly sales volumes of over 84 thousand metric tons of LCE'

company_snapshot.claim: In October 2026 SQM presented a unified 'SQM Group' corporate identity grouping SQM, Novandino Litio and SQM Litio Internacional, launched at events in Santiago, Antofagasta and Iquique.
company_snapshot.so_what: A group-wide umbrella makes it easier to carry a success from one division (iodine) into another (lithium).
company_snapshot.verification_note: S23 (29 Oct 2026): 'eventos en Santiago, Antofagasta e Iquique ... nuevo nombre corporativo que agrupa SQM, Novandino Litio y SQM Litio Internacional'

findings.claim: In 2024 SQM reorganised into three divisions: SQM Litio Chile, SQM Litio Internacional and SQM Yodo-Nutrición Vegetal (2024 Annual Report chair's letter).
findings.so_what: The 'Northern Operations Division' named in the email does not match a public division name, so the BDR should confirm which business unit (Novandino lithium or Iodine-Plant Nutrition) Rodrigo sits in.
findings.verification_note: S17 letter: 'reorganización corporativa que dio lugar a tres divisiones: SQM Litio Chile, SQM Litio Internacional y SQM Yodo-Nutrición Vegetal'

findings.claim: Novandino's board has three Codelco directors (Máximo Pacheco, chair; Josefina Montenegro; Alfredo Moreno) and three SQM directors (Ricardo Ramos, vice chair; Hernán Uribe; Manuel Ovalle), with Carlos Díaz, previously general manager of SQM Litio, as general manager and Codelco's Eduardo Foix as finance manager.
findings.so_what: Large spend at the Atacama sites will pass a JV governance with a Codelco-appointed finance manager, which may lengthen the paper process.
findings.verification_note: S8/S12 board names; S12: 'eligieron a Pacheco como presidente y a Ramos ... como vicepresidente'; S13: 'gerente general de SQM Litio, Carlos Díaz, en el cargo de gerente general de Nova Andino, y a Eduardo Foix de Codelco como su gerente de Finanzas'

findings.claim: Diario Financiero reported that Novandino's executive team under Carlos Díaz includes a salar operations manager (Gilbert Maldonado), a lithium operations manager (Humberto Carvajal), a maintenance and automation manager (Gerson Salas), a supply chain manager (Germán Pérez) and, under VP José Miguel Berguño, a digitalisation and IT manager (Andrés Pinto) and a risk management superintendency (Luis Acuña).
findings.so_what: These are the operations, automation, IT, procurement and risk roles a drone-in-a-box programme must win over.
findings.verification_note: S12: 'Gilbert Maldonado, gerente de operaciones salar'; 'Humberto Carvajal, gerente de operaciones litio'; 'Gerson Salas, gerente de mantenimiento y automatización'; 'Germán Pérez, gerente supply chain'; under Berguño: 'gerente de digitalización y TI, Andrés Pinto' and 'Superintendencia de Gestión de Riesgos liderada por Luis Acuña'

findings.claim: The 3,533 SQM Litio workers moved to Novandino, working from the same offices; SQM retains operational and administrative continuity until 2030, after which the state becomes majority partner with 50% plus one share.
findings.so_what: The operating teams Rodrigo works with are stable through 2030, so a multi-year programme is not disrupted by the JV transition.
findings.verification_note: S13: 'los 3.533 trabajadores de la filial SQM Litio' 'desde las mismas oficinas'; transition to 2030, 'todo seguirá igual para SQM Litio, incluso en lo administrativo'; then 'el Estado pasará a ser el socio mayoritario ... 50% más una acción'

findings.claim: FlytBase's SQM case study names Rodrigo Toler as Deputy Manager of Digital Innovation at SQM, and a November 2025 FlytBase webinar lists him as Deputy Manager, M1+ Digital, SQM.
findings.so_what: An internal SQM champion of autonomous drones already exists and can be a reference for the lithium team.

budget_signals.claim: In its 2Q2026 earnings release (August 2026), SQM guided capital expenditures of about US$3 billion for 2026-2028, roughly 60% for Novandino, 20% for Iodine and Plant Nutrition and 20% for International Lithium, including about US$300 million per year of sustaining capex across all divisions.
budget_signals.so_what: About US$1.8 billion of planned capex goes to Novandino, plus a sustaining budget each year, which is where an inspection-automation line item would fit.
budget_signals.verification_note: S10 2Q2026 release (call 19 Aug 2026): 'approximately US$3 billion ... 2026 to 2028 ... 60% for Novandino, 20% ... Iodine and Plant Nutrition ... 20% ... International Lithium ... US$300 million per year of sustaining'

budget_signals.claim: In November 2025 SQM cut its 2025-2027 capex estimate to US$2.7 billion from a previous US$3.1-3.8 billion, delaying some investment decisions while keeping production and sales targets, with about 25% allocated to maintenance.
budget_signals.so_what: SQM is capital-disciplined, so pitch a low-capex, fast-payback programme and lead with opex savings rather than a large upfront investment.
budget_signals.verification_note: S9 (Nov 19 2025): 'US$2.7 billion from a previous range of $3.1-$3.8 billion ... delayed some investment decisions, but maintained its production and sales targets ... about a quarter going to maintenance'; S7 confirms

budget_signals.claim: The 2025 Annual Report chair's letter says SQM invested more than US$876 million in 2025 in strategic projects, including lithium expansions in Chile; the 2024 letter said SQM invested more than US$1,300 million in 2024 and projected about US$1,100 million for 2025.
budget_signals.so_what: Actual 2025 spend was below the plan made a year earlier, which confirms careful spending and the need for a clear ROI case.
budget_signals.verification_note: S18: 'destinando en 2025 más de US$876 millones ... incluyendo expansiones de litio en Chile'; S17: 'en 2024 destinamos más de US$1.300 millones ... Para 2025, proyectamos una inversión cercana a US$1.100 millones'

recent_news.claim: In July 2026 Novandino submitted the environmental impact study for 'Operational Continuity and Future Mining Development in the Salar de Atacama' (Salar Futuro), a US$3 billion plan to extend operations from 2031 to 2060 with forced evaporation, nanofiltration, direct lithium extraction and reverse osmosis.
recent_news.so_what: The company is publicly committed to new technology at the salar, which makes autonomous inspection fit its innovation story.

recent_news.so_what: Tighter extraction limits and monitoring raise the value of frequent, repeatable data on wells, ponds and sensitive areas.

recent_news.so_what: Field and contractor exposure at the salar is under regulatory scrutiny, which supports the safety case for fewer people walking the site.

positioning_recommendation.summary: Position FlytBase as the proven SQM autonomy platform moving from Iodine to Novandino's lithium operations, not as a new vendor. The iodine programme with Adentu (daily autonomous missions, 95%+ reliability, ROI under a year on a USD 70-80k system) speaks directly to SQM's stated focus on operational excellence, innovation and financial discipline. Offer a one-site pilot at the salar ahead of the Q3 budget discussion, aimed at pond and well inspection and the stricter environmental monitoring commitments, and show the safety and contractor-cost savings. Bring Adentu as the local partner and Rodrigo Toler's team as the internal reference.
angles: Internal proof: the same company and desert already run FlytBase with Adentu, with inspection going from biweekly to twice daily and ROI under a year [S1][S11][S20]
Scale of the salar: 4,550 ha of evaporation ponds and 403 wells are a natural fit for scheduled drone-in-a-box patrols instead of crews on foot [S25]
Compliance: the April 2026 RCA requires updated monitoring with higher frequency in sensitive sectors, which scheduled autonomous flights can support [S24]
Safety: the February 2026 Labour Directorate suspension of work and of a contractor at SQM Salar over outdoor-worker conditions supports reducing field exposure [S21]

Budget fit: about 60% of the US$3bn 2026-2028 capex goes to Novandino, with about US$300M a year of sustaining capex, so position the programme as low-capex and fast-payback in line with SQM's capex discipline [S10][S7][S9]
24/7 operations: SQM's security department already ordered docks for 24/7 surveillance, a template for the contact's 24/7 lithium sites [S1][S11]
risks_or_objections: Governance: the Atacama sites belong to the Codelco-SQM JV with a Codelco-appointed finance manager, so procurement and approval may involve more parties than an SQM-only purchase [S12][S13]
The contact's 'Northern Operations Division' and the '3 sites' could not be matched to public org data; confirm the business unit and which assets are meant (salar, Carmen plant or iodine sites)
Capex discipline: SQM cut and delayed investments in late 2025, so a large upfront hardware request may stall [S7][S9]

Community sensitivity: the Salar Futuro EIA declares a significant impact on Atacameño ancestral territory, with traffic-control and non-interference measures, so flight paths near the east border may need community consideration [S15]
Harsh site conditions (altitude around 2,300 m, temperature swings) and BVLOS still on the roadmap in the iodine deployment may limit initial coverage [S21][S1]
